# Abstract

This gazetteer documents the 90-site settlement inventory of the Cumberland (Tennessee) Hydrological Unit (HU 06; 110.698 km²) from 8200BC to 1600AD.
Out of 186 candidate sites audited in the regional source ledger, 90 archaeological river-bluff camps, shell middens, palisaded mound towns and Cherokee settlements (53 in Tennessee, 25 in Alabama, 6 in North Carolina, 4 in Kentucky, 1 in Illinois and 1 in Virginia) are retained in the gazetteer, while 96 candidates (94 duplicate-alias consolidations within 2 km and 2 unquantified non-habitation limestone cave exclusions: Dust Cave and Russell Cave) are excluded.
Catalogued centres span from Early Holocene river-bluff and terrace sites (Rose Island 8200BC-7000BC, Stanfield-Worley Bluff Shelter 8000BC-2000BC, Icehouse Bottom 7500BC-750AD and Eva 6000BC-1500BC) and Middle Woodland ceremonial hubs (Florence Mound 480, Old Stone Fort 480, Garden Creek 440) to Mississippian and Overhill Cherokee towns led by Kincaid Mounds (2,4k at 1300AD), Hiwassee Island Town (1,3k at 1300AD), Hiwassee Island (1,2k at 1400AD), Toqua Dallas Town (1,2k at 1450AD), Jonathan Creek Palisaded Town (1,1k at 1350AD), Savannah Mound Town (1,1k at 1300AD), Shiloh Indian Mounds (1,1k at 1200AD), Toqua (1,1k at 1400AD), Muscle Shoals Town (1k at 1300AD) and Hobbs Island Town (950 at 1350AD).

# Background

Excavations across the Tennessee, Little Tennessee, Hiwassee and Elk valleys reveal a multi-stage shift in settlement nucleation between 8200BC and 1600AD [@griffin1974; @lewis1946; @welch2006].
Early and Middle Archaic foraging bands returned seasonally to river-bluff terraces and shell-mound shoals at Rose Island, Icehouse Bottom, Stanfield-Worley Bluff Shelter, Eva and Seven Mile Island [@griffin1974], before Middle Woodland communities erected ceremonial stone walls and earthen mounds at Old Stone Fort, Florence Mound and Oakville Indian Mounds.
During the twelfth and thirteenth centuries (1100AD-1300AD), large Mississippian platform-mound towns flourished across both the lower river (Kincaid Mounds, Shiloh Indian Mounds, Jonathan Creek) and Middle Tennessee (Hobbs Island, Kogers Island) [@welch2006; @muller1997].

By 1400AD-1500AD, Vacant Quarter depopulation abandoned the lower and middle reaches [@cobb2002; @cobb2023], shifting demographic weight toward Dallas, Mouse Creek and early Cherokee towns across the Ridge-and-Valley and Appalachian foothills (Hiwassee Island, Toqua, Citico, Dallas, Ledford Island, Citico (Overhill), Tomotley, Kituhwa, Nikwasi and Coweeta Creek) [@polhemus1987; @schroedl1986; @lewis1946].
These upland communities maintained close exchange and political ties with adjacent Coosa, Etowah and Appalachian contact-era paramountcies recorded by sixteenth-century Spanish expeditions [@king2003; @hudson1997; @beck2016].

# Methodology

## Inclusion Criteria and Schema Audit

All 186 candidate sites in the regional source ledger were audited for surveyed WGS84 coordinates, dated residential or plaza area series and distinct geographic bounds.
Ninety-four overlapping coordinate-alias entries within 2 km of canonical sites were consolidated alongside 2 unquantified non-habitation limestone cave exclusions (Dust Cave and Russell Cave), leaving 90 unique included settlements in the gazetteer.
All retained records carry canonical CENTAUR provenance, reserving detailed monograph citations for this gazetteer and the ledger.

## Mound-Town Population Calibration

Town headcounts integrate palisade-enclosed domestic zone areas, excavated wall-trench house counts (5-6 occupants per structure adjusted for timber replacement spans) and sixteenth-century Spanish household chronicles where documented across neighbouring Appalachian chiefdoms [@polhemus1987; @muller1997; @hudson1997; @beck2016].
Early Holocene river-bluff and terrace occupations (Rose Island, Icehouse Bottom and Stanfield-Worley Bluff Shelter) follow hearth-area foraging group multipliers (50-75 occupants at peak) calibrated against radiocarbon-dated occupational strata, whereas unquantified limestone cave deposits (Dust Cave and Russell Cave) are held out of point totals [@griffin1974; @kelly2025].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation between the settlement gazetteer and the regional source ledger passed with 0 unaccounted candidates and 0 coordinate or schema errors at GMT+0:

1. **Included Settlements**: 90 sites (40 in Upper East Tennessee and Ridge-and-Valley, 28 in Middle Tennessee Bend and Muscle Shoals, and 22 in the Lower Tennessee-Kentucky confluence), whose individual peaks sum to 52,3k (Table \ref{tab:cu-summary}).
2. **Excluded Candidates**: 96 entries (94 duplicate-alias consolidations within 2 km and 2 non-habitation cave exclusions, Dust Cave and Russell Cave, making 186 candidates total).

# Results

## Top 45 Archaic, Mississippian and Cherokee Centres

Out of 90 catalogued settlements, Table \ref{tab:cu-included} lists the top 45 centres ranked by peak population descending, from Kincaid Mounds (2,4k at 1300AD) down to Paris Landing Village (530 at 1350AD), omitting the remaining 45 smaller towns and camps (from Big Sandy River Village at 520 down to Stanfield-Worley Bluff Shelter at 50) to preserve compact single-gazetteer table pagination.
Figure \ref{fig:cu-settlements} charts the rank-size distribution across all 90 settlements and the leading 15 sites.
Along the Middle and Lower Tennessee, Kincaid Mounds peaks at 2,4k (1300AD), Jonathan Creek Palisaded Town at 1,1k (1350AD), Savannah Mound Town at 1,1k (1300AD), Shiloh Indian Mounds at 1,1k (1200AD), Muscle Shoals Town at 1k (1300AD), Hobbs Island Town at 950 (1350AD), Jonathan Creek at 920 (1200AD), Seven Mile Island Town at 850 (1350AD) and Link Duck River Town at 800 (1350AD) prior to Vacant Quarter abandonment [@welch2006; @cobb2002; @cobb2023].

In Upper East Tennessee and the Blue Ridge valleys, Hiwassee Island Town peaks at 1,3k (1300AD), Hiwassee Island at 1,2k (1400AD), Toqua Dallas Town at 1,2k (1450AD), Toqua at 1,1k (1400AD), Citico at 920 (1400AD), Moccasin Bend Habitation Town at 900 (1350AD), Dallas at 740 (1450AD), Ledford Island at 690 (1500AD) and Rymer at 540 (1500AD) [@lewis1946; @polhemus1987].
Early Overhill and Middle Cherokee centres continue through 1600AD, led by Citico (Overhill) (780), Tomotley (750 at 1500AD), Kituhwa (680), Nikwasi (620) and Coweeta Creek (480 at 1550AD) [@schroedl1986; @hudson1997].
Linearly interpolated across active site occupation spans in the 90-site corpus, catalogued settlements sum to 21,2k in 1200AD, 31,2k in 1300AD, 16,3k in 1400AD, 13,6k in 1500AD and 6,03k in 1600AD.

# Limitations

Frontier overlap places borderland capitals such as Kincaid Mounds (along the Ohio River edge in southern Illinois) and Kituhwa and Nikwasi (along the Little Tennessee headwaters) within the HU 06 gazetteer perimeter; mosaic reconciliation with HU 03 (Southeast) and HU 05 (Ohio River) prevents double-counting in continental pixel sums.
In addition, twentieth-century reservoir flooding beneath Tennessee Valley Authority impoundments submerged unexcavated bottomland hamlets, leaving dispersed farmsteads represented through sub-regional rural carrying capacities rather than individual site rows [@welch2006; @cobb2023].
